findings.evidence: https://harborview-clinic.test/ (page type home). H1 is 'Welcome'. The first 400 characters of observed content read: "Welcome We are proud to serve the community with care and compassion." | "Our doors have been open for many years and we continue that tradition every single day." | "It has always been our belief that patients deserve better.". None of these names an audience or an outcome - no phrase of the form "for <who>", "helps <who> <do what>", or "<product> is a <category>" appears. A first-time visitor has to infer what this is.

suggested_action.mechanism: A visitor decides whether to stay from the first screen; without a sentence that names them, they have to do the work of inferring relevance, and most leave instead.
suggested_action.summary: Open with one sentence naming the audience and the outcome.

findings.evidence: https://harborview-clinic.test/contact (page type contact) marks these as required: phone, company, job_title, dob, address1, postcode. A visitor at this stage has not yet been given anything, so personal or organisational detail is being demanded before any value is delivered. On a checkout or application page these same fields would be necessary and this check does not fire there.

suggested_action.mechanism: Fields that feel invasive relative to what is being offered cause abandonment at the field itself, not at submission.
suggested_action.patch:
<input name="phone" type="tel">  <!-- required attribute removed -->
<input name="company" type="text">  <!-- required attribute removed -->
<input name="job_title" type="text">  <!-- required attribute removed -->
<input name="dob" type="date">  <!-- required attribute removed -->
<input name="address1" type="text">  <!-- required attribute removed -->
<input name="postcode" type="text">  <!-- required attribute removed -->
suggested_action.summary: Make phone, company, job_title, dob, address1, postcode optional, or move them to a later step.

findings.evidence: The brand name 'Home' is a single short generic word. Within 10 words of the name on https://harborview-clinic.test/ there is no descriptor saying what kind of thing it is, and no schema description supplies one. A system that encounters this name elsewhere has nothing to tie it back to this organisation.

suggested_action.mechanism: A descriptor beside the name gives a disambiguating anchor, so statements about this entity can be separated from statements about others sharing the name.
suggested_action.patch:
Home is a __FILL_IN__:category for __FILL_IN__:audience, based in __FILL_IN__:location.

"description": "__FILL_IN__:one_line_category_description", "sameAs": ["__FILL_IN__:wikidata_or_wikipedia_url", "__FILL_IN__:linkedin_url"]
suggested_action.source: Handout appendix, Why agreement across the web matters
suggested_action.summary: Put a category descriptor next to the name, and add sameAs links.
suggested_action.verification: Search the exact name and see whether this organisation is the first unambiguous result; if not, the descriptor is doing no work yet.

findings.evidence: https://harborview-clinic.test/ declares 0 sameAs link(s), of which 0 point at an independent identity source such as Wikipedia, Wikidata, Companies House, LinkedIn or GitHub. Across 4 crawled pages the site links outward to 0 distinct external host(s). This says what we observed ON THIS SITE. It is not evidence that no one else mentions the brand, which cannot be established from the site alone, so this finding is reported at likely confidence and never as confirmed.

suggested_action.mechanism: sameAs states that this site and an independent record describe one entity, which lets a checker corroborate a claim here against a source elsewhere instead of taking it on trust.
suggested_action.patch:
"sameAs": [
  "__FILL_IN__:wikidata_or_wikipedia_url",
  "__FILL_IN__:linkedin_company_url",
  "__FILL_IN__:github_or_crunchbase_url"
]
<!-- Only list profiles that genuinely describe this same entity. -->
suggested_action.source: schema.org/sameAs; handout appendix, Why agreement across the web matters
suggested_action.summary: Add sameAs links from your Organization node to profiles you already control.

findings.evidence: https://harborview-clinic.test/contact (page type contact) posts to /send with 13 visible fields against a threshold of 8 for this site type. Fields, with * marking required: first_name:text*, last_name:text*, email:email*, phone:tel*, company:text*, job_title:text*, dob:date*, address1:text*, address2:text, city:text*, postcode:text*, referrer:text, message:text. Hidden and submit inputs were excluded from the count.

suggested_action.mechanism: Every field is a separate decision and a separate chance to abandon; fields that are not needed to fulfil the request cost completions without returning anything.
suggested_action.patch:
<form action="/send" method="post">
  <label for="email">__FILL_IN__:label_text</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required>
  <button type="submit">__FILL_IN__:verb_plus_object</button>
</form>
<!-- Collect the remaining detail after the visitor has received something. -->
suggested_action.summary: Ask only for what is needed to deliver the next step; collect the rest later.

limitations.confidence_effect: not assessed; re-run with --probe-bot-ua to close this gap
limitations.reason:
Edge and CDN reachability for named AI crawlers was not assessed, because --probe-bot-ua was not set. This is the highest-value check in this marketplace: a CDN or WAF rule that returns 403 to OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot or Claude-SearchBot removes a brand from those assistants entirely, and leaves no trace in robots.txt or in what a human sees. If you own this site, re-run the orchestrator with the --probe-bot-ua flag:
    orchestrate.py <url> --out ./audit-output --probe-bot-ua
That sends ONE request per crawler, to the homepage only, with an auditor token appended to the user-agent string so it is identifiable in your logs. It is off by default because sending named-crawler user-agents to a site you do not own is not something an audit should do without being asked.
